title: He didn’t die so you could stay comfortable.
paragraphs: He didn’t die so you could stay comfortable.
He died so you could become new.

That’s the weight of Luke 9:23. Jesus never marketed discipleship like a softer life, a safer road, or an easier story. He said, “If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.” The cross was not jewelry. It was death to the old life.

That means Jesus is not just trying to reduce your stress.
He is trying to crucify your pride.

Not just calm your fears.
But break your chains.

Not just improve your habits.
But give you a new heart.

We love a Savior who rescues.
But many resist a Savior who rules.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because the call to deny yourself is not a call to earn love. It is the result of being loved by Christ. He saves you first. Then He changes you. The old you—driven by flesh, ego, lust, bitterness, applause—must go. And in Christ, a new creation rises.

Yes, following Jesus will cost you.
Your sin.
Your excuses.
Your double life.
Your throne.

But what He gives is better:
new life,
new desires,
new identity,
new hope.
So no—Jesus didn’t come to make life easier.
He came to make dead people live.
